cards.explanation: The answer is a colt, friends. Jesus tells the two disciples they'll find one tied there, in the village ahead of them. They go and find it just as He told them (Luke 19:32).
The answer is True! Jesus says it's a colt “…on which no one has ever sat.” That's a very specific detail to give two people who haven't even left yet. And then, just as He said, they find it.

The answer is “The Lord needs it.” Jesus says, “If anyone asks, ‘Why are you untying it?’ tell him, ‘The Lord needs it.’…” Short and simple, the kind of answer you could say with a straight face. And when the owners do ask, the disciples answer, “The Lord needs it.” word for word (Luke 19:34).

The answer is owners, friends! The colt's owners asked the disciples, “Why are you untying the colt?” (Luke 19:33). Somebody noticed what they were doing. Good thing the disciples already had their answer ready.
The answer is their cloaks, friends! Luke 19:35 says they “…threw their cloaks over it, and put Jesus on it.” Cloaks first, then Jesus. That's the order the text gives.

The answer is all the miracles they had seen. The whole multitude of disciples praises God joyfully “…for all the miracles they had seen…” They weren't praising Him for something they'd heard about secondhand. They'd seen it with their own eyes, and they couldn't keep it in.

The answer is The King! The crowd of disciples shouts, “Blessed is the King who comes in the name of the Lord!” That's a big title to call out loud on a public road. And the one on the colt is the one they're calling it to.

The answer is rebuke! Some of the Pharisees in the crowd say, “Teacher, rebuke Your disciples!” They call Him Teacher and then ask Him to correct the crowd. That's the request. I think they were hoping for a quiet ride.

The answer is the very stones! Jesus says, “I tell you, if they remain silent, the very stones will cry out.” Think about that, friends. Even stones get a voice in that sentence. That's a big answer to a small request.

The answer is wept. Luke 19:41 says that as Jesus approached Jerusalem and saw the city, He wept over it. I think this one hurts a little, friends. First the crowd praises God, then the text shows Jesus weeping.

The answer is True. Jesus says, “If only you had known on this day what would bring you peace! But now it is hidden from your eyes.” He's talking to the city, and it's a heavy thing to say. I think He says it with tears still on His face, since He just wept over it.

The answer is that the city did not recognize God's visit. That's the reason Jesus gives. He says it will come “…because you did not recognize the time of your visitation from God.” Not a mystery, friends, He tells them plainly. The reason sits right at the end of His words.
